investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official events listing page (Contao CMS, 'Veranstaltungen'), plus two events' own 'Kalender-Eintrag' links, which turned out to actually be per-event ICS files (Content-Type: text/calendar) served under a '.html'-suffixed URL. One of the two was re-fetched a second time to empirically check UID stability.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official 'Veranstaltungen' listing page (https://columbiahalle.berlin/veranstaltungen.html) immediately exposed 87 distinct upcoming event entries as fully server-rendered static HTML, grouped under month/year headings ('August 2026'), each event row itself stating only weekday+day-of-month (not month/year). Each event's own 'Kalender-Eintrag' link resolved directly to a per-event ICS file (Content-Type: text/calendar) with a full UTC DTSTART/DTEND, LOCATION, GEO, and a UID matching the listing page's own event_<id> HTML anchor. Re-fetching the same ICS a second time confirmed the UID is stable, not regenerated per request. No JSON-LD, WordPress, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present, and none was needed.

venue_reference: Columbiahalle (mid-large concert hall, Tempelhof/Kreuzberg border, Columbiadamm, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained listing page's own <title> reads 'Columbiahalle - Veranstaltungen - deutsch' at the venue's own domain columbiahalle.berlin. Independently, the retained per-event ICS states its own LOCATION as 'Columbiahalle, Columbiadamm 13-21, 10965 Berlin' with a matching GEO coordinate (52.4845171, 13.3905217) and a UID suffix '@Columbiahalle' — a second, distinct retained artifact confirming the same identity.

site_classification.platform: Contao CMS (identifiable by 'ce_text block' content-element markup) with a calendar/event extension. The full upcoming-events listing is server-rendered on one static page, grouped by month/year heading with day-only event rows. Each event additionally exposes its own per-event ICS export at a '.html'-suffixed URL (Content-Type: text/calendar), a routing quirk of this Contao calendar module rather than a real HTML detail page.

title.notes:
The listing row's own

Elle & L's Festival

and the ICS's own SUMMARY both state the title directly.

start_date.notes:
The event's own listing row states only weekday+day-of-month ('Samstag, 29') — the month/year is established once by the nearest preceding

August 2026

heading, which governs every row beneath it until the next such heading. Combining 'August 2026' + '29' via the fixed rule ' ' + '' -> '--
' yields exactly one result. Independently corroborated by the per-event ICS's own directly-stated DTSTART (20260829T130000Z = 15:00 CEST on 2026-08-29), which alone would already be DIRECT_SOURCE for this specific record — the DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT basis is recorded here because it is the listing page's own general per-row pattern this collector family would need to rely on across all 87 events, most of which were not individually ICS-sampled.

derivation.rule:
The nearest preceding month/year heading ('

Month Year

' inside an 'eventlist_monat' block) governs every event row that follows it until the next such heading; the row's own weekday+day-of-month text supplies the day. Concatenate as --
.

time.notes: The listing row directly states local 'Beginn: 15:00 Uhr' (Europe/Berlin). The per-event ICS independently and directly states the same instant as a full UTC timestamp (DTSTART 20260829T130000Z = 15:00 CEST). Recorded value is the ICS's own explicit UTC instant.

end.notes: The per-event ICS directly states its own DTEND (20260829T220000Z). Unlike the AEG-operated Berlin venues already investigated (verti-music-hall-berlin-01, uber-arena-berlin-01), where DTEND was a suspicious fixed DTSTART+2h on every sampled event, this source's two sampled events show a genuinely variable DTSTART-to-DTEND gap (Elle & L's Festival: 9h; badmómzjay: 4h) — consistent with a real, source-maintained end time rather than a synthesized default.

venue_location.notes: The per-event ICS directly states its own LOCATION and GEO fields on every VEVENT — a genuinely per-record, directly-stated fact.

source_record_id.notes: The per-event ICS's own UID field ('9702@Columbiahalle'), matching the listing page's own 'id="event_9702"' HTML anchor for the same record — a source-authored identifier, not merely something that looks numeric/stable. Empirically re-fetched the same event's ICS a second time (evidence ev-ics-elle-refetch) and confirmed the UID is identical across both fetches (only DTSTAMP, a generation timestamp, differed) — satisfying the policy's stable-identifier rule by empirical proof, not assumption. This differs from the known Hot Clube de Portugal ICS UID-regeneration failure mode documented in docs/OBSERVATION_PIPELINE.md.

event_url.notes: The per-event ICS's own URL field states this record's own canonical anchor link back to the listing page.

price.notes: The listing row shows only a 'VVK: ab 35,00 €' (advance-sale, starting-from) price string per event — a real, directly-stated value, but a lower-bound indicator rather than a complete price/tier breakdown, and this field is not present at all in the ICS export. Not promoted to a single proven price value.

blockers.description: Per-event ICS URLs were only discovered via the listing page's own 'Kalender-Eintrag' link per event (a two-step crawl: list page -> per-event ICS), not a single bulk feed covering all 87 events at once. A future collector would need to enumerate all 'veranstaltung/*.html' links from the listing page first, then fetch each one's ICS — still entirely Level 1 static, just not a single-request bulk export.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from two independently retained artifacts (listing page title, and the ICS's own LOCATION/GEO/UID-domain text).
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the full 87-event listing page plus two sampled per-event ICS files (one re-fetched to prove UID stability).
title and start_date both PROVEN — title via DIRECT_SOURCE, start_date via DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT with a stated mechanical rule and >=2 cited inputs.
source_record_id PROVEN via the ICS's own stable UID, empirically confirmed stable across two independent fetches.
end and venue_location additionally PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE via the ICS's own DTEND/LOCATION/GEO fields — stronger than either AEG-operated sibling investigation.
recommended_family ICS_CALENDAR, an existing documented collector family — no new family required.
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (only one MINOR blocker noting the two-step crawl needed to enumerate per-event ICS URLs).

Not advanced to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: (1) no DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence item exists yet for the DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT start_date field (gate 9/v1.2 offline-proof requirement), and (2) only 2 of 87 listed events were individually ICS-sampled — that broader reproduction and offline proof are separate follow-up work, not performed as part of this investigation task.
